The must-sees

10 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Neighbourhood

    Alberta Street

    Many of its buildings were designed by Mikhail Eisenstein in the early 1900s. Riga has one of the largest collections of Art Nouveau architecture in Europe.

    Look for

    Look high on the facades, above the doors: Eisenstein put giant screaming faces, masks and creatures up near the roofline.

  2. 02
    Building · 1909

    Cat House

    A local tale says the owner, kept out of the Great Guild, first turned the cats’ tails toward the guild hall. The house was built in 1909.

    Look for

    Look across to the Great Guild hall nearby, the building the cats are said to have turned their tails on.

  3. 03
    Landmark · 1935

    Freedom Monument

    Paid for by public donations and unveiled in 1935, it was designed by Kārlis Zāle. Under Soviet rule it was never torn down, and it became the gathering point of the independence movement.

    Look for

    Read the words on the base: “Tēvzemei un Brīvībai”, For Fatherland and Freedom.

  4. 04
    Building

    House of the Blackheads

    The original was used by the Brotherhood of Blackheads, a guild of unmarried merchants. Destroyed in 1941, its walls were cleared away by the Soviets, and it was rebuilt in time for Riga’s 800th anniversary in 2001.

    Look for

    On the facade, find the brotherhood’s emblem: the dark-skinned head of its patron saint, St Maurice, which gave the Blackheads their name.

  5. 05
    Museum

    Museum of the Occupation of Latvia

    It tells of the Soviet and Nazi German occupations of Latvia between 1940 and 1991. Deportations to Siberia are a central part of the story.

    Look for

    Inside, letters, photographs and belongings tell the stories of Latvians deported to Siberia.

  6. 06
    Palace

    Riga Castle

    It was founded by the Livonian Order in the 14th century and rebuilt many times. A fire in 2013 damaged part of it, and it has since been restored.

  7. 07
    Church

    Riga Cathedral

    Bishop Albert laid its foundation in 1211. Its organ, built by the Walcker firm in 1884, was among the largest in the world at the time.

    Look for

    Notice that you step down to the doors: the streets around the cathedral have risen over the centuries.

  8. 08
    Market

    Riga Central Market

    The pavilions were built in the 1920s and 1930s reusing German First World War Zeppelin hangars. It is one of the largest markets in Europe.

    Look for

    Look up beyond the halls to the tall Stalin-era tower of the Latvian Academy of Sciences.

  9. 09
    Church

    St. Peter’s Church

    First mentioned in 1209, it has lost its spire several times to fire and collapse. The present spire was rebuilt in the 1970s after the church burned in 1941.

  10. 10
    Building

    Three Brothers

    Each comes from a different century; the oldest is thought to be the oldest dwelling house in Riga. They now house the Latvian Museum of Architecture.

    Look for

    The white house with the stepped gable, number 17, is the oldest, from the 15th century. The narrow green one, number 21, is the youngest.
